page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. No marginal notes. Catchword at the foot, right.

main_text.p: fallorum invicem exortum. ut Aurum & Argen-tum.
Aurum est metallum ortum, omnium perfectis-simum, ex sulphure & mercurio, ad summa puritatem, subtilitatem, atq; æquabilitate redactis.
Hinc colore flavo nitente præditum est: quoq; magis ad rubedinem splendente accedit, nobilius est; perfectiore coctione ostendens partium.
Est etiam gravissimum, maximeq; ductile: ob artissimam complexionem & subtilitatem partium, quâ fit, ut minimi ejus sint pori. Quare etiam aliis metallis minus est sonorum.
Argentum est metallum perfectum, secundum aurum purissimum, ex artissimâ mercurii sulphurisq; albicantium partium conjunctione.
unde albore nitente conspicuum est: valdeq; ductile & grave.
Imperfectiora metalla, ex debiliori coctione sulphuris & argenti vivi: sunt, Plumbum & Stannum.
Plumbum, ex multo argento vivo parùm coĉto, & immundo sulphure.
Ex quo colorem ex albo fuscū contraxit, maximeq; est liquatile,
Stannum autem, ex mercurio albo & sulphure non probè commixto natum, colore albo, majorèq; quàm plumbum duritie præditum.

page.notes: The printed line "maiorèq;" is partly unclear (first letters look like "jor"), so the reading "majorèq;" is doubtful. The word "perfectis-simum" is split at a line end; the letters before the hyphen are not fully clear. The first line "fallorum invicem exortum" continues the previous page, and "tum." is the end of the broken heading "Argentum". The closing line "Hæc de metallis purioribus." is centred italic and is treated as a closing sentence, not a heading. The catchword "tio-" stands at the lower right.
